body:
Three contributions are before me. The account made the memory gap primary and prescribed a shared record, a weekly check-in, and a separate approach to the avoiding friend. The objection held that the ordering was not forced, that the account slipped between forgetting and genuine disagreement about terms, and that its proposed test could not discriminate. The rival added two readings of its own — divergence at the moment of agreement, and arguments as renegotiation of standing — plus a cheap probe to run before anything is installed. What follows is my adjudication: what I use, revise, leave open, and reject.

I take up, as the firmest gain of the exchange, the distinction between drift and divergence. The objection made it as memorial versus normative disagreement; the rival made the same cut differently — did the meaning change after the agreement, or was it never shared at the moment of speaking? Two independent criticisms converging on one distinction is the strongest ground available for keeping it, and it matters practically, because the remedies fork: drift is helped by a record, while 'A: dishes, Mon' is exactly as interpretable as 'I'll do the dishes' and so does nothing for divergence. The account's best textual support is the problem's own phrasing — 'we agree... later we disagree' — which sounds temporal. But the objection conceded more than it needed to when it granted that the material supports the retrospective drift claim: the rival's second reading shows even that is underdetermined, because latent divergence surfaces later too. Two sincere hearers of 'this week' and 'every week' discover the difference only when it bites, and from inside it looks exactly like drift.

What I reject is not the record but its unconditional form, and the check-in as a first move. A note without scope stated at the moment of agreement relocates the dispute onto the note (the rival's point); a weekly meeting assumes the group conversation can happen, which is precisely what the avoidance puts in question (the objection's point). What survives of the account is conditional: if drift is what shows, a forward-looking record of fresh agreements is proportionate — never a retrospective one, which would be re-litigation with paperwork.

What I revise is the rival's probe. I keep its shape: ask each flatmate separately, before installing any system, what they understood one specific recent agreement to mean. Three amendments. First, ask about a particular agreement, not agreements in general — the rival's own caveat is that recollection is what's in dispute, and specificity narrows the room for reconstruction. Second, add a behavioral anchor: when did you first notice the mismatch, and what was happening with schedules around then? Drift should track schedule changes and elapsed time; divergence should bite even on fresh agreements made under stable schedules. Third, keep the rival's framing for the avoiding friend — ask their reading of a chore agreement, not about their avoidance — and include them. That answers the rival's worry that a private conversation makes their withdrawal the topic; a question about a chore is the lowest-stakes available version, and it quietly tests whether bilateral conversation is possible at all.

One thing none of the inputs stated plainly: the asker is inside the dispute. The account flagged the coalition risk for the one-to-one, but the same logic applies to every conversation the asker initiates, including the probe — any diagnostic run by an interested party is also a move in the game it observes. The mitigation is cheap but not a control: state your own reconstruction first, marked as a reconstruction, and ask at a moment not adjacent to a fresh argument.

The objection charged that the account's test could be read as support under any outcome. The repair is not a better outcome measure but advance prediction, and I state mine now: if disputes persist about agreements whose scope was explicitly stated at the time, that counts for the normative or standing readings and against mere ambiguity, and I will not read it as a failure of note-keeping. If fresh, scoped agreements run clean while old ones still rankle, that is drift being cleared. If answers do not cluster on any dimension and the same task re-disputes after explicit settlement, the standing-reading gets its first real support. Here I must also flag what looks like an inversion in the objection's own pre-registered falsifier: as written, it counts a result against itself that its own analysis predicts. Unless I have misread it, the coherent mirror — the outcome that genuinely tells against the objection's avoidance-central ordering — is the intervention working: scoped agreements running clean and the avoiding friend re-engaging. I adopt the corrected version.

What I leave open: the standing-reading, which the rival itself conceded it had not evidenced beyond a caution; the mediator, which no input could rank from the material and neither can I — I can only name the trigger, which is even the low-stakes bilateral ask producing withdrawal; and the load distribution and the avoidance's history, which the material never states and I will not fill.

For the asker, this week: one specific question to each flatmate in turn, including the avoiding one, framed as curiosity about an agreement rather than about anyone's conduct. Everything else — the record, the habit of scope-stating, any group conversation — waits on what comes back.
commitments:
Taking this up involves several separable things.

The drift/divergence distinction is now the load-bearing claim, and it commits whoever uses it to the practical fork: a forward record only if drift shows, a habit of stating scope aloud if divergence shows. If practice shows the two cannot be separated — if writing a scope down is itself what forces the norm into the open, the possibility the objection anticipated — the fork collapses into doing both cheap habits at once. I would count that a revision rather than a refutation, but it removes my reason for probing before prescribing, and I accept that consequence.

The revised probe is a proposal with known limits. It reaches current reports, not past understandings; the behavioral anchor is a mitigation, not a fix. I inherit the rival's caveat: non-clustering answers must not be read as confirming whichever reading the asker already held. I add my own: the asker is a party, so answers given to them are shaped by that, and 'own reconstruction first, stated as a reconstruction' is a courtesy, not a control. If the probe returns nothing decisive, that is an admissible outcome, not a failed one.

The advance predictions are pre-registrations, and I commit to the least flattering reading of the first: disputes persisting despite explicit scoping will be treated as evidence for the normative or standing readings, not as insufficient note-keeping. Symmetrically, and this is the corrected mirror of what I take to be the objection's inverted falsifier: if scoped fresh agreements run clean and the avoiding friend re-engages, the avoidance-central ordering loses and I will say so rather than explain it away as temporary compliance.

Sequencing commitments: no weekly check-in before the bilateral probe has happened; no retrospective record ever; any record forward-looking only. These are droppable — if the flatmates themselves want a chart or rota, their preference overrides my ordering and the probe can run alongside it. My rejection of the unconditional record is on sequencing grounds, not on evidence that records fail; the rival explicitly did not show that a record makes things worse, and I do not claim to have shown it either.

I take no position on and will not fill: how the load is distributed, whether the avoidance predates the schedule changes, or whether arguments are escalating. The standing-reading remains a hypothesis; its first real support would be non-clustering answers plus re-dispute after explicit settlement plus avoidance that is about the conversations rather than the chores. The mediator remains unrankable; I name only the trigger — even the low-stakes bilateral ask producing withdrawal — and cannot say whether a mediator or any other route is better if it fires.

Finally, a criticism I could be wrong about: I read the objection's pre-registered falsifier as inverted and adopted a corrected version. If the objection actually meant what it wrote — if there is a reading on which continuing arguments support the memory-gap account — I would need that shown. Until then my correction stands as an interpretation of one sentence, not a verdict on the objection as a whole, most of which I have taken up rather than set aside.
